## plotnine Examples {#sec-plotnine-examples}

**maidr** also supports [plotnine](https://plotnine.org/), the Python
implementation of ggplot2's grammar of graphics. Pass a `ggplot` to
`maidr.show()`, `maidr.render()` or `maidr.save_html()`, and **maidr** produces
a page where the chart can be read from the keyboard, as sound, as text and in
braille -- what [maidr for R](https://r.maidr.ai/) does for ggplot2 itself. For
the other libraries, see the
[Matplotlib / Seaborn](examples.qmd), [Plotly](examples-plotly.qmd),
[Bokeh](examples-bokeh.qmd) and [Altair](examples-altair.qmd) pages.

::: {.callout-warning title="Experimental"}
plotnine support is **experimental**. What it reads, and how, may change without
a deprecation period, whichever plot type is drawn: see
[Plot Type Stability](stability.qmd#plotnine-support). Install it with
`pip install "maidr[plotnine]"`.
:::

**maidr** reads each layer's own data as plotnine computed it -- after the
stat, the position adjustment and the scales -- rather than the shapes it drew,
so a count is the count `stat_count` made, a stacked segment is announced with
its own value, and a box with the five numbers `stat_boxplot` computed. Each
facet panel is a subplot. As you move through a chart, the mark being read is
outlined on the plotnine drawing itself.

| plotnine | read as |
|---|---|
| `geom_bar`, `geom_col`, one bar per category | bar |
| `geom_bar`, `geom_col` with `position="stack"` (the default) | stacked bar |
| `geom_bar`, `geom_col` with `position="dodge"` | dodged bar |
| `geom_histogram` | histogram |
| `geom_point` | point |
| `geom_line` | line, one series per group |
| `geom_smooth` | smooth, with its confidence band |
| `geom_boxplot` | box |
| `geom_tile` with a numeric `fill` | heatmap |
| `facet_wrap`, `facet_grid` | one subplot per panel |
| `geom_bar`, `geom_col` with `position="fill"` | normalized stacked bar [experimental] |

Any other geom, a jittered point, or a chart on a coordinate system other than
`coord_cartesian` is left out with a warning naming it, and a chart with
nothing **maidr** can read is shown as a static image. Use `maidr.show(p)`
rather than plotnine's own `p.show()` or a notebook's display of `p`: those draw
the chart as an ordinary matplotlib figure, which **maidr** cannot read beyond
its points.

### Bar Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Bar chart of the number of penguins of each species

from plotnine import aes, geom_bar, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(penguins, aes("species"))
    + geom_bar()
    + labs(title="Penguins per Species", x="Species", y="Penguins")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Stacked Bar Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Stacked bar chart of penguins per species, split by island

from plotnine import aes, geom_bar, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(penguins, aes("species", fill="island"))
    + geom_bar()
    + labs(title="Penguins per Species and Island", x="Species", y="Penguins")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

Each segment is announced with its own count, not the height of the stack it
sits on, and a species with no penguins on an island is announced as missing
rather than as zero. The series run from the bottom of the stack up.

### Dodged (Grouped) Bar Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Grouped bar chart of penguins per species, one bar for each sex

from plotnine import aes, geom_bar, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(penguins.dropna(subset=["sex"]), aes("species", fill="sex"))
    + geom_bar(position="dodge")
    + labs(title="Penguins per Species and Sex", x="Species", y="Penguins")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Histogram

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Histogram of penguin body mass in twenty bins

from plotnine import aes, geom_histogram, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(penguins.dropna(subset=["body_mass_g"]), aes("body_mass_g"))
    + geom_histogram(bins=20)
    + labs(title="Penguin Body Mass", x="Body Mass (g)", y="Penguins")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Scatter Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Scatter plot of penguin bill length against bill depth

from plotnine import aes, geom_point, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(penguins.dropna(), aes("bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm"))
    + geom_point()
    + labs(title="Bill Length and Depth", x="Bill Length (mm)", y="Bill Depth (mm)")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Line Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Line chart of monthly US unemployment from 1967 to 2015

from plotnine import aes, geom_line, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import economics

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(economics, aes("date", "unemploy"))
    + geom_line()
    + labs(title="US Unemployment", x="Month", y="Unemployed (thousands)")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Multi-Line Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Two lines, the personal savings rate and the median weeks of unemployment

from plotnine import aes, geom_line, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import economics_long

import maidr  #<<

two = economics_long[economics_long["variable"].isin(["psavert", "uempmed"])]
p = (
    ggplot(two, aes("date", "value", color="variable"))
    + geom_line()
    + labs(title="Savings Rate and Unemployment Duration", x="Month", y="Value")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

Each colour is one series, named by its value of the variable `color` maps.

### Box Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Box plots of penguin body mass for each species

from plotnine import aes, geom_boxplot, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(penguins.dropna(subset=["body_mass_g"]), aes("species", "body_mass_g"))
    + geom_boxplot()
    + labs(title="Body Mass by Species", x="Species", y="Body Mass (g)")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

### Heatmap

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Heatmap of mean penguin body mass for each species on each island

from plotnine import aes, geom_tile, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

means = (
    penguins.groupby(["species", "island"], observed=True)["body_mass_g"]
    .mean()
    .round()
    .reset_index()
)
p = (
    ggplot(means, aes("island", "species", fill="body_mass_g"))
    + geom_tile()
    + labs(title="Mean Body Mass (g)", x="Island", y="Species", fill="Body Mass (g)")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

Each cell is announced with the value `fill` maps, not its colour. A species
never recorded on an island has no tile, and is announced as missing.

### Scatter Plot with a Smooth

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Scatter plot of flipper length against body mass with a fitted line and its confidence band

from plotnine import aes, geom_point, geom_smooth, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(penguins.dropna(), aes("flipper_length_mm", "body_mass_g"))
    + geom_point()
    + geom_smooth(method="lm")
    + labs(title="Flipper Length and Body Mass", x="Flipper Length (mm)",
           y="Body Mass (g)")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

The points and the fitted line are two layers of one subplot; the line carries
the bounds of its confidence band at every point.

### Faceted Plot

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Three scatter plots side by side, bill length against bill depth for each species

from plotnine import aes, facet_wrap, geom_point, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(penguins.dropna(), aes("bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm"))
    + geom_point()
    + facet_wrap("species")
    + labs(title="Bills by Species", x="Bill Length (mm)", y="Bill Depth (mm)")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

Each panel is a subplot, titled by its facet as `species = Adelie`. Press
<kbd>Enter</kbd> to go into one, <kbd>Escape</kbd> to come back out, and the
arrow keys between them, in the directions they are laid out on the page.

### Normalized Stacked Bar Plot [experimental]

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: Stacked bar chart of the share of each species on each island

from plotnine import aes, geom_bar, ggplot, labs
from plotnine.data import penguins

import maidr  #<<

p = (
    ggplot(penguins, aes("island", fill="species"))
    + geom_bar(position="fill")
    + labs(title="Species Share on Each Island", x="Island", y="Share")
)

maidr.show(p)  #<<
```

Each segment is announced as its share of the bar, so the segments of one bar
add up to 1.

## Saving and embedding

`maidr.save_html(p, "chart.html")` writes the same page to a file, and
`maidr.render(p)` returns it as HTML for a Shiny or Streamlit app. plotnine
draws through matplotlib, so `use_cdn` behaves exactly as it does for a
matplotlib figure, and `use_cdn=False` gives a page that works offline.
